scope: National Lung Screening Trial: low-dose CT versus chest radiography, with the reported relative reduction in lung-cancer mortality.

keyRecommendations.text: Low-dose CT screening produced a relative reduction in mortality from lung cancer of 20.0% (95% CI 6.8 to 26.7) compared with chest radiography.
Death from any cause was reduced by 6.7% (95% CI 1.2 to 13.6) in the low-dose CT group compared with the radiography group.

clinicalBottomLine: In the NLST, low-dose CT reduced lung-cancer mortality by a relative 20.0% versus chest radiography, and all-cause mortality by 6.7%. The comparator was radiography, not no screening.
notableCaveats: The PMC text is the public author manuscript. USPSTF eligibility is a separate topic and is not restated as an NLST result.

source.title: Reduced lung-cancer mortality with low-dose computed tomographic screening.
